```{r}
library(changepoint)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# Fonction pour appliquer cpt.meanvar avec différentes pénalités
apply_cpt_meanvar <- function(data, penalties) {
  results <- list()
  for (penalty in penalties) {
    tryCatch({
      changepoint <- cpt.meanvar(data, method = "PELT", penalty = penalty)
      results[[penalty]] <- changepoint
    }, error = function(e) {
      message(sprintf("Error with penalty %s: %s", penalty, e$message))
    })
  }
  return(results)
}

# Fonction pour évaluer la qualité du modèle
evaluate_model <- function(data, changepoint) {
  segments <- cpts(changepoint)
  n <- length(data)
  
  # Calculer la somme des carrés des résidus
  rss <- sum((data - rep(param.est(changepoint)$mean, diff(c(0, segments, n))))^2)
  
  # Calculer le BIC
  k <- length(segments) + 1  # nombre de segments
  bic <- n * log(rss/n) + k * log(n)
  
  # Calculer l'AIC
  aic <- n * log(rss/n) + 2 * k
  
  return(list(rss = rss, bic = bic, aic = aic, num_changes = k-1))
}

# Fonction principale
analyze_changepoints <- function(data, penalties) {
  # Appliquer cpt.meanvar avec différentes pénalités
  results <- apply_cpt_meanvar(data, penalties)
  
  # Évaluer chaque modèle
  evaluations <- lapply(results, function(x) evaluate_model(data, x))
  
  # Créer un dataframe avec les résultats
  eval_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(evaluations), function(penalty) {
    data.frame(
      penalty = penalty,
      rss = evaluations[[penalty]]$rss,
      bic = evaluations[[penalty]]$bic,
      aic = evaluations[[penalty]]$aic,
      num_changes = evaluations[[penalty]]$num_changes
    )
  }))
  
  # Trouver la meilleure pénalité basée sur le BIC
  best_penalty <- eval_df$penalty[which.min(eval_df$bic)]
  
  # Visualiser les résultats
  p <- ggplot(eval_df, aes(x = penalty)) +
    geom_point(aes(y = bic, color = "BIC")) +
    geom_point(aes(y = aic, color = "AIC")) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("BIC" = "blue", "AIC" = "green")) +
    labs(title = "Critères d'information vs Pénalité",
         x = "Pénalité", y = "Valeur du critère") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  
  print(p)
  
  return(list(evaluations = eval_df, best_penalty = best_penalty))
}

# Utilisation
penalties <- c("SIC", "BIC", "AIC", "MBIC", "MAIC", "Hannan-Quinn", "Asymptotic", "Manual")
results <- analyze_changepoints(Burel$vehicle, penalties)

# Afficher les résultats
print(results$evaluations)
cat("Meilleure pénalité:", results$best_penalty)

# Appliquer le modèle final avec la meilleure pénalité
final_model <- cpt.meanvar(Burel$vehicle, method = "PELT", penalty = "MBIC")

# Visualiser les points de rupture
plot(final_model)
```

```{r}
# Fonction pour créer des données aberrantes et retourner les dates des outliers
create_outliers <- function(data, segment_id, type = "vehicle", percent = 1, proportion = 0.05) {
  data_copy <- data
  # Filtrer les données pour le segment spécifié
  segment_data <- data_copy %>% filter(segment_id == !!segment_id)
  
  # Sélectionner aléatoirement une proportion de lignes
  n_outliers <- floor(nrow(segsegment_data) * proportion)
  outlier_indices <- sample(1:nrow(segment_data), n_outliers)
  
  # Augmenter ou diminuer les valeurs de 30%
  segment_data$outliers <- segment_data[[type]]
  segment_data$outliers[outlier_indices] <- segment_data[[type]][outlier_indices] * 
    (1 + sample(c(-1, 1), n_outliers, replace = TRUE) * percent)
  
  # Mettre à jour les données avec les outliers
  data_copy[data_copy$segment_id == segment_id, type] <- segment_data$outliers
  
  data_copy$imputed[outlier_indices] <- "Modified"
  return(data_copy)
}
```

```{r}
analyze_traffic <- function(data, segment_id, start_date = NULL, end_date = NULL, type = "vehicle") {
  library(dplyr)
  library(zoo)
  library(changepoint)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(plotly)
  library(purrr)


  # Filtrer les données pour le segment spécifié
  segment_data <- data %>% filter(segment_id == !!segment_id)
  
  # Filtrer les données pour la période spécifiée
  if (!is.null(start_date)) {
    segment_data <- segment_data %>% filter(date >= !!start_date)
  }
  if (!is.null(end_date)) {
    segment_data <- segment_data %>% filter(date <= !!end_date)
  }
  
  # Vérifier si le type de véhicule est valide
  if (!(type %in% colnames(segment_data))) {
    stop("Transport type does not exist in the data")
  }
  
  # Enregistrer le type de transport comme colonne à analyser
  segment_data <- segment_data %>% rename(transport = !!type)
  
  segment_name <- unique(segment_data$segment_name)
  
  # Appliquer le lissage
  smoothed_data <- rollmean(segment_data$transport, k = 7, fill = TRUE, align = "center")
  
  # Appliquer PELT sur les données lissées
  model_mbic <- cpt.meanvar(smoothed_data, method = "PELT", penalty = "MBIC")
  changepoints <- cpts(model_mbic)
  
  # Fonction pour fusionner les périodes courtes
  merge_short_periods <- function(changepoints, data) {
    periods <- diff(c(0, changepoints, nrow(data)))
    merged <- c()
    i <- 1
    while (i <= length(periods)) {
      if (periods[i] < 24 && i < length(periods)) { # Moins d'un jour (24 heures)
        # Calculer les moyennes des périodes adjacentes
        mean_current <- mean(data$transport[(sum(periods[1:(i-1)]) + 1):(sum(periods[1:i]))])
        mean_next <- mean(data$transport[(sum(periods[1:i]) + 1):(sum(periods[1:(i+1)]))])
        mean_prev <- if(i > 1) mean(data$transport[(sum(periods[1:(i-2)]) + 1):(sum(periods[1:(i-1)]))]) else Inf
        
        # Fusionner avec la période la plus proche en moyenne
        if (abs(mean_current - mean_prev) <= abs(mean_current - mean_next) && i > 1) {
          periods[i-1] <- periods[i-1] + periods[i]
          periods <- periods[-(i)]
        } else {
          periods[i+1] <- periods[i] + periods[i+1]
          periods <- periods[-(i)]
        }
      } else {
        i <- i + 1
      }
    }
    return(cumsum(periods)[-length(periods)])
  }
  
  # Appliquer la fusion des périodes courtes
  changepoints <- merge_short_periods(changepoints, segment_data)
  
  date_changepoints <- segment_data$date[changepoints]
  
  # Créer un dataframe pour la visualisation
  df_plot <- segment_data %>%
    mutate(changepoint = ifelse(row_number() %in% changepoints, "Yes", "No"))
  
  # Plot PELT
  plot_pelt <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = date, y = round(transport,0))) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(date_changepoints), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("PELT Changepoints for Segment", segment_name),
         x = "Time", y = paste(type, "Count"))
  
  plot_pelt <- ggplotly(plot_pelt)
  
  # Boxplots
  segments <- split(df_plot, cumsum(df_plot$changepoint == "Yes"))
  
  # Définition de la fonction identify_outliers à l'intérieur de analyze_traffic
  identify_outliers <- function(x) {
    q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25)
    q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75)
    iqr <- q3 - q1
    lower_bound <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
    upper_bound <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr
    return(x < lower_bound | x > upper_bound)
  }
  
  # Préparation des données pour les boxplots
  boxplot_data <- map_dfr(seq_along(segments), ~{
    segment <- segments[[.x]]
    segment %>% mutate(period = paste0("P", .x))
  })
  
  # Identifier les outliers pour chaque période
  boxplot_data <- boxplot_data %>%
    group_by(period) %>%
    mutate(is_outlier = identify_outliers(transport)) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Calculer les informations de période
  period_info <- boxplot_data %>%
    group_by(period) %>%
    summarise(
      start_date = min(date),
      end_date = max(date),
      n_days = as.numeric(round(difftime(max(date), min(date), units = "days"),0))
    )
   # Ajouter le nombre d'outliers par période
  n_outliers <- boxplot_data %>%
    filter(is_outlier) %>%
    group_by(period) %>%
    summarise(n_outliers = n())
  
  legend_df <- period_info %>%
    left_join(n_outliers, by = "period") %>%
    replace_na(list(n_outliers = 0))
  
  #Trier les périodes  par start_date 
  legend_df <- legend_df %>% arrange(start_date)
  # Créer le boxplot avec ggplot2
  plot_boxplot <- suppressWarnings(
    ggplot(boxplot_data, aes(x = factor(period, levels = unique(period)), y = transport)) +
    geom_boxplot(outliers = F, fill = "lightblue") +  
    geom_point(data = subset(boxplot_data, is_outlier), 
               aes(text = paste("Date:", format(date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
                                "<br>Vehicle Count:", round(transport,0),
                                "<br>Imputed:", imputed),
                   color = as.factor(imputed)),  # Utilisez aes() ici
               size = 1.5) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Traffic Periods for", segment_name),
         x = "Period", y = "Vehicle Count") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  )
  
  plot_boxplot <- ggplotly(plot_boxplot, tooltip = "text")

  
  # Créer une table pour la légende
  legend_table <- plot_ly(
    type = 'table',
    header = list(values = c("Period", "Start", "End", "Days", "Outliers"),
                  align = c("left", "center", "center", "center", "center"),
                  line = list(width = 1, color = 'black'),
                  fill = list(color = 'grey'),
                  font = list(family = "Arial", size = 10, color = "white")),
    cells = list(values = list(legend_df$period, format(legend_df$start_date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), format(legend_df$end_date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), legend_df$n_days, legend_df$n_outliers),
                 align = c("left", "center", "center", "center", "center"),
                 line = list(color = "black", width = 1),
                 font = list(family = "Arial", size = 9))
  )
  
  # Combiner les graphiques
  combined_plot <- subplot(
    list(plot_pelt, plot_boxplot),
   nrows = 2
  ) %>% 
    layout(
      title = paste("Traffic Analysis for Segment", segment_name)
    )
  
  result <- list(plot= combined_plot, table = legend_table ,period = period_info)
  return(result)
}

# Utilisation de la fonction
unique_segments <- unique(dataV2$segment_id)
list_result <- list()

for (id in unique_segments) {
  tryCatch({
    result <- suppressMessages(analyze_traffic(dataV2, id,type = "vehicle"))
    list_result[[as.character(id)]] <- result
    
    # Afficher les graphiques
    print(result$plot)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Erreur pour le segment_id", id, ":", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  })
}
```

```{r}
analyze_traffic_period <- function(data, segment_id, data_period, type = "vehicle") {
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(plotly)
  library(purrr)
  
  # Filtrer les données pour le segment spécifié
  segment_data <- data %>% filter(segment_id == !!segment_id)
  
  # Vérifier si le type de véhicule est valide
  if (!(type %in% colnames(segment_data))) {
    stop("Transport type does not exist in the data")
  }
  
  # Enregistrer le type de transport comme colonne à analyser
  segment_data <- segment_data %>% rename(transport = !!type)
  
  segment_name <- unique(segment_data$segment_name)
  
  # Assurer que les dates sont dans le bon format
  segment_data <- segment_data %>% 
    mutate(date = as.POSIXct(date, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC")) %>%
    arrange(date)
  
  data_period <- data_period %>%
    mutate(start_date = as.POSIXct(start_date, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC"),
           end_date = as.POSIXct(end_date, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC")) %>%
    arrange(start_date)
  
  # Fonction pour attribuer un segment à chaque date
  assign_segment <- function(date, periods) {
    for (i in 1:nrow(periods)) {
      if (date >= periods$start_date[i] && date <= periods$end_date[i]) {
        return(i)
      }
    }
    return(NA)
  }
  
  # Appliquer la fonction à chaque date dans segment_data
  segment_data <- segment_data %>%
    mutate(segment = sapply(date, assign_segment, periods = data_period))
  
  # Vérifier s'il y a des NA dans la colonne segment
  if (any(is.na(segment_data$segment))) {
    warning("Certaines dates n'ont pas pu être assignées à un segment.")
  }
  
  # Diviser les données en segments
  segments <- split(segment_data, segment_data$segment)
  
  # Plot PELT
  plot_pelt <- ggplot(segment_data, aes(x = date, y = round(transport, 0))) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(data_period$start_date), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("PELT Changepoints for Segment", segment_name),
         x = "Time", y = paste(type, "Count"))
  
  plot_pelt <- ggplotly(plot_pelt)
  
  # Définition de la fonction identify_outliers à l'intérieur de analyze_traffic_period
  identify_outliers <- function(x) {
    q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25,na.rm=T)
    q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75,na.rm=T)
    iqr <- q3 - q1
    lower_bound <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
    upper_bound <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr
    return(x < lower_bound | x > upper_bound)
  }
  
  # Préparation des données pour les boxplots
  boxplot_data <- map_dfr(seq_along(segments), ~{
    segment <- segments[[.x]]
    segment %>% mutate(period = paste0("P", .x))
  })
  
  # Identifier les outliers pour chaque période
  boxplot_data <- boxplot_data %>%
    group_by(period) %>%
    mutate(is_outlier = identify_outliers(transport)) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Calculer les informations de période
  period_info <- boxplot_data %>%
    group_by(period) %>%
    summarise(
      start_date = min(date),
      end_date = max(date),
      n_days = as.numeric(round(difftime(max(date), min(date), units = "days"), 0))
    )
  
  # Ajouter le nombre d'outliers par période
  n_outliers <- boxplot_data %>%
    filter(is_outlier) %>%
    group_by(period) %>%
    summarise(n_outliers = n())
  
  legend_df <- period_info %>%
    left_join(n_outliers, by = "period") %>%
    replace_na(list(n_outliers = 0))
  
  # Trier les périodes par start_date 
  legend_df <- legend_df %>% arrange(start_date)
  
  # Créer le boxplot avec ggplot2
 plot_boxplot <- suppressWarnings(
    ggplot(boxplot_data, aes(x = factor(period, levels = unique(period)), y = transport)) +
    geom_boxplot(outliers = F, fill = "lightblue") +  
    geom_point(data = subset(boxplot_data, is_outlier), 
               aes(text = paste("Date:", format(date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
                                "<br>Vehicle Count:", round(transport,0),
                                "<br>Imputed:", imputed),
                   color = as.factor(imputed)),  # Utilisez aes() ici
               size = 1.5) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Traffic Periods for", segment_name),
         x = "Period", y = "Vehicle Count") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  )
 
  
  plot_boxplot <- ggplotly(plot_boxplot, tooltip = "text")
  
  # Créer une table pour la légende
  legend_table <- plot_ly(
    type = 'table',
    header = list(values = c("Period", "Start", "End", "Days", "Outliers"),
                  align = c("left", "center", "center", "center", "center"),
                  line = list(width = 1, color = 'black'),
                  fill = list(color = 'grey'),
                  font = list(family = "Arial", size = 10, color = "white")),
    cells = list(values = list(legend_df$period, format(legend_df$start_date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), format(legend_df$end_date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), legend_df$n_days, legend_df$n_outliers),
                 align = c("left", "center", "center", "center", "center"),
                 line = list(color = "black", width = 1),
                 font = list(family = "Arial", size = 9))
  )
  
  # Combiner les graphiques
  combined_plot <- subplot(
    list(plot_pelt, plot_boxplot),
    nrows = 2
  ) %>% 
    layout(
      title = paste("Traffic Analysis for Segment", segment_name)
    )
  
  result <- list(plot = combined_plot, table = legend_table)
  return(result)
}
```

```{r}

analyze_traffic_combined <- function(data, segment_id, start_date = NULL, end_date = NULL, type = "vehicle") {
  library(dplyr)
  library(zoo)
  library(changepoint)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(plotly)
  library(purrr)

  # Filtrer les données pour le segment spécifié
  segment_data <- data %>% filter(segment_id == !!segment_id)
  
  # Filtrer les données pour la période spécifiée
  if (!is.null(start_date)) {
    segment_data <- segment_data %>% filter(date >= !!start_date)
  }
  if (!is.null(end_date)) {
    segment_data <- segment_data %>% filter(date <= !!end_date)
  }
  
  # Vérifier si le type de véhicule est valide
  if (!(type %in% colnames(segment_data))) {
    stop("Transport type does not exist in the data")
  }
  

  
  
  segment_name <- unique(segment_data$segment_name)
  
  # Créer une copie des données non imputées
  segment_data_non_imputed <- segment_data %>% mutate(vehicle = car + heavy) %>% 
    rename(transport = !!type) %>% filter(uptime_quality)
  
  # Imputer les données manquantes
  segment_data_imputed <- impute_missing_data(segment_data,transport_type = type ) %>% rename(transport = !!type)
  print(segment_data_imputed %>% filter(imputed == "imputed"))
  # Appliquer le lissage sur les données imputées
  smoothed_data <- rollmean(segment_data_imputed$transport, k = 7, fill = NA, align = "center")
  
  # Supprimer les NA du début et de la fin pour PELT
  smoothed_data_clean <- na.omit(smoothed_data)
  
  # Appliquer PELT sur les données lissées et nettoyées
  model_mbic <- cpt.meanvar(smoothed_data_clean, method = "PELT", penalty = "MBIC")
  changepoints <- cpts(model_mbic)
  
  # Ajuster les points de changement pour correspondre aux indices originaux
  first_non_na <- which(!is.na(smoothed_data))[1]
  changepoints <- changepoints + first_non_na - 1
  
  # Fonction pour fusionner les périodes courtes
  merge_short_periods <- function(changepoints, data) {
    periods <- diff(c(0, changepoints, nrow(data)))
    merged <- c()
    i <- 1
    while (i <= length(periods)) {
      if (periods[i] < 24 && i < length(periods)) { # Moins d'un jour (24 heures)
        # Calculer les moyennes des périodes adjacentes
        mean_current <- mean(data$transport[(sum(periods[1:(i-1)]) + 1):(sum(periods[1:i]))], na.rm = TRUE)
        mean_next <- mean(data$transport[(sum(periods[1:i]) + 1):(sum(periods[1:(i+1)]))], na.rm = TRUE)
        mean_prev <- if(i > 1) mean(data$transport[(sum(periods[1:(i-2)]) + 1):(sum(periods[1:(i-1)]))], na.rm = TRUE) else Inf
        
        # Vérifier que les moyennes ne sont pas NA
        if (!is.na(mean_current) && !is.na(mean_next) && !is.na(mean_prev)) {
          # Fusionner avec la période la plus proche en moyenne
          if (abs(mean_current - mean_prev) <= abs(mean_current - mean_next) && i > 1) {
            periods[i-1] <- periods[i-1] + periods[i]
            periods <- periods[-(i)]
          } else {
            periods[i+1] <- periods[i] + periods[i+1]
            periods <- periods[-(i)]
          }
        } else {
          i <- i + 1
        }
      } else {
        i <- i + 1
      }
    }
    return(cumsum(periods)[-length(periods)])
  }

  # Appliquer la fusion des périodes courtes
  changepoints <- merge_short_periods(changepoints, segment_data_imputed)
  
  date_changepoints <- segment_data_imputed$date[changepoints]
  
  # Créer un dataframe pour la visualisation
  df_plot <- segment_data_imputed %>%
    mutate(changepoint = ifelse(row_number() %in% changepoints, "Yes", "No"))
  
  # Plot PELT
  plot_pelt <- ggplot() +
    geom_line(data = df_plot, aes(x = date, y = round(transport, 0))) +
    geom_point(data = df_plot, aes(x = date, y = round(transport, 0), color = as.factor(imputed)), size = 0.65) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(date_changepoints), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("PELT Changepoints for Segment", segment_name),
         x = "Time", y = paste(type, "Count"))

  plot_pelt <- ggplotly(plot_pelt)
  
  # Préparation des données pour les boxplots
  all_breaks <- c(min(segment_data_imputed$date), date_changepoints, max(segment_data_imputed$date))
  
  assign_period <- function(date, breaks) {
    period <- findInterval(date, breaks)
    return(paste0("P", period))
  }
  
  boxplot_data_imputed <- segment_data_imputed %>%
    mutate(period = sapply(date, assign_period, breaks = all_breaks))
  
  boxplot_data_non_imputed <- segment_data_non_imputed %>%
    mutate(period = sapply(date, assign_period, breaks = all_breaks))
  
  # Identifier les outliers pour chaque période et type de données
  identify_outliers <- function(x) {
    q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
    q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
    iqr <- q3 - q1
    lower_bound <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
    upper_bound <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr
    return(x < lower_bound | x > upper_bound)
  }
  
  boxplot_data_imputed <- boxplot_data_imputed %>%
    group_by(period) %>%
    mutate(is_outlier = identify_outliers(transport)) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  boxplot_data_non_imputed <- boxplot_data_non_imputed %>%
    group_by(period) %>%
    mutate(is_outlier = identify_outliers(transport)) %>%
    ungroup() 
  
  # Créer le boxplot pour les données imputées
  plot_boxplot_imputed <- suppressWarnings(
    ggplot(boxplot_data_imputed, aes(x = factor(period, levels = unique(period)), y = transport)) +
    geom_boxplot(outliers = F, fill = "indianred2") +  
    geom_point(data = subset(boxplot_data_imputed, is_outlier), 
               aes(text = paste("Date:", format(date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
                                "<br>Vehicle Count:", round(transport,0),
                                "<br>Imputed:", imputed),
                   color = as.factor(imputed)), 
               size = 1.5) +
    theme_minimal()  +
    labs(title = paste("Traffic Periods for", segment_name, "(Imputed Data)"),
         x = "Period", y = "Vehicle Count") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)))
    
  plot_boxplot_imputed <- ggplotly(plot_boxplot_imputed, tooltip = "text")

  # Créer le boxplot pour les données non imputées
plot_boxplot_non_imputed <- suppressWarnings(
    ggplot(boxplot_data_non_imputed, aes(x = factor(period, levels = unique(period)), y = transport)) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", outliers = FALSE) +
    geom_point(data = subset(boxplot_data_non_imputed, is_outlier), 
               aes(text = paste("Date:", format(date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
                                "<br>Vehicle Count:", round(transport, 0)))) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Traffic Periods for", segment_name, "(Non-Imputed Data)"),
         x = "Period", y = "Vehicle Count") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
)

plot_boxplot_non_imputed <- ggplotly(plot_boxplot_non_imputed, tooltip = "text")
# Calculer les informations de période pour les données imputées
period_info <- boxplot_data_imputed %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(
    start_date = min(date),
    end_date = max(date),
    n_days = as.numeric(round(difftime(max(date), min(date), units = "days"), 0)),
    n_total_data = n(),
    n_original_data = sum(imputed == "original"),
    n_imputed_data = n_total_data - n_original_data,  # Nombre de données imputées
    pct_imputed = ifelse(n_total_data == 0, 0, round(100 * n_imputed_data / n_total_data, 2)),  # Éviter la division par zéro
    n_outliers_after_imputation = sum(ifelse(is_outlier, 1, 0)),  # Nombre d'outliers après imputation
    n_imputed_outliers = sum(ifelse(is_outlier & imputed == "imputed", 1, 0)),  # Nombre d'outliers imputés
    n_outliers_original = n_outliers_after_imputation - n_imputed_outliers
  ) %>%
  arrange(start_date)

# Remplacer les NA par 0 pour les colonnes numériques
period_info[is.na(period_info)] <- 0

# Calculer le pourcentage de données imputées par période
period_info <- period_info %>%
  mutate(
    pct_imputed = ifelse(is.na(pct_imputed), 0, pct_imputed),  # Remplacer les NA par 0
    n_imputed_data = ifelse(is.na(n_imputed_data), 0, n_imputed_data)
  )

# Calculer les outliers avant imputation
n_outliers_before_imputation <- boxplot_data_non_imputed %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(ifelse(is_outlier, 1, 0))) %>%
  arrange(start_date)

# Créer une table pour la légende
legend_table <- plot_ly(
  type = 'table',
  header = list(values = c("Period", "Start", "End", "Days", "Total Data", "Original Data", "Imputed Data", "% Imputed", "Outliers (Before Imputation)", "Outliers (After Imputation)", "Outliers (Original)", "Imputed Outliers"),
                align = c("left", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center"),
                line = list(width = 1, color = 'black'),
                fill = list(color = 'grey'),
                font = list(family = "Arial", size = 10, color = "white")),
  cells = list(values = list(period_info$period, 
                             format(period_info$start_date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), 
                             format(period_info$end_date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), 
                             period_info$n_days,
                             period_info$n_total_data,
                             period_info$n_original_data,
                             period_info$n_imputed_data,
                             period_info$pct_imputed,
                             n_outliers_before_imputation$n,
                             period_info$n_outliers_after_imputation,
                             period_info$n_outliers_original,
                             period_info$n_imputed_outliers),
               align = c("left", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center", "center"),
               line = list(color = "black", width = 1),
               font = list(family = "Arial", size = 9))
)

  # Combiner les graphiques
  combined_plot <- subplot(
    list(plot_pelt, plot_boxplot_imputed, plot_boxplot_non_imputed),
    nrows = 3
  ) %>% 
    layout(
      title = paste("Traffic Analysis for Segment", segment_name)
    )
  
  result <- list(plot = combined_plot, table = legend_table)
  return(result)
}
```
